01 · PUBLISHED ACCOUNT

Monsoon and state growth

Under active examination

Can the documented climate sequence produce a decline in Angkor’s political core?

What we tested
We ran 2,000 matched parameter draws at each of three crop responses, plus a neutral-climate comparison.
What we learned
At the middle response, 1,260 of 2,000 runs decline; their median onset is 1362. Changing crop sensitivity shifts the timing.
What remains open
The PDSI-to-harvest translation is assumed. Core activity combines court presence and regional population.
Explore model →Read the research ↗

02 · ECOLOGY AND MOBILISATION

Can an army return before harvest?

Under active examination

How do distance, fish and labour demands change what the landscape can support?

What we tested
Six scenarios, each with 32 matched seeds and 18 simulated years.
What we learned
Moving the frontier from 180 to 540 km adds 40 campaign days and creates harvest overlap in every modeled year.
What remains open
Unbounded stores mask food pressure in the default setup. Historical quantities still need review.
Explore model →Read the research ↗

03 · AUTHORITY AND ALLEGIANCE

What does a monument persuade people to believe?

Under active examination

Can inherited stone keep tribute flowing after military capacity weakens?

What we tested
Matched comparisons change how suppliers read stone, elephants and defence.
What we learned
Default suppliers pledge during failed defence for 7.28 of 12 years on average. Lower trust reduces that to 2.34.
What remains open
This result tests our belief rule. The numerical relationship has yet to be established historically.
Explore model →Read the research ↗

04 · OBLIGATIONS AND EXIT

Who pays when the court leaves?

Under active examination

How do temple bills, court costs and interrupted deliveries affect exit and return?

What we tested
The model consumes pledges from the signalling experiment and compares return rules.
What we learned
With the same interruption, 21 of 32 courts exit. Allowing a funded return brings all 21 back.
What remains open
Two consecutive shortfalls trigger exit by assumption. Return also depends on assumed funding rules.
Explore model →Read the research ↗

EDUCATION · LABOUR MARKETS

China’s graduate queue

Next research focus

What happens when graduates compete for a limited pool of secure jobs?

What we tested
Browser and Python outputs were checked for parity; the app compares the model with the supplied NBS series.
What we learned
The earlier 2018–22 fit missed the later unemployment bulge. Matching the displayed record leaves the mechanisms open.
What remains open
The reporting definition changes in 2024. Several labour-market responses are assumptions.
Explore model →Read the research ↗

EDUCATION · SCHOOL AND WORK

School and child labour in Cambodia

In progress

How might school costs, protection, meals and enforcement affect children’s work?

What we tested
Policy and reference runs use the same starting seed across 12 simulated years.
What we learned
The interface exposes differences between policies. Causal policy effects remain under examination.
What remains open
Programme effect sizes are stylised, and the rural school-retention fit needs a large unexplained adjustment.
Explore model →Read the research ↗

PLANNING · REFERENCE METHOD

Can teacher supply keep up?

Synthetic demonstration

When do training delays and departures create a teacher shortage?

What we tested
An age-structured accounting model follows intake, graduation, hiring and retirement through 2050.
What we learned
Explore how a lag between training decisions and hiring changes the projected gap.
What remains open
Starting counts and completion rates are synthetic. This demonstration carries no country forecast.

ANGKOR · A GUIDED RECONSTRUCTION

How does this society work?

Start with food and labour. Follow how the existing experiments turn resources into growth, infrastructure and authority, then examine what happens when commitments or climate change.

The models and their boundaries

These are existing experiments with different time scales and accounting boundaries. The guide connects their questions. The signalling-to-obligations handoff carries settings and pledges; other connections remain conceptual.

A curve that rises and falls tests the equations that produced it. Historical support comes from comparing population, construction, land use and upkeep with independent evidence, while tracking adjustable assumptions.

Published foundation · Temple communities

How did temple communities provision a city?

Begin with Klassen, Ortman, Lobo and Evans: coordinated production, spatial equilibrium and the growth of the archaeological sample. The model reproduces normalized relationships from their paper.

Open the published economic foundation →

1 · Provision the landscape

What feeds the people who build and fight?

Rice and fish supply households. Grain and work time also pay for campaigns, channels and construction. The court collects a share after the village reserve.

Open this step →

2 · Follow growth through time

How can production support a larger settlement?

The existing water-and-rice model follows a synthetic regional population through time. Harvests depend on yield and infrastructure condition; population responds within that framework.

Open this step →

3 · Turn resources into authority

What does visible construction tell a tributary?

The court inherits monuments and elephants, then divides resources between new construction and a military response. A supplier decides whether to pledge tribute using visible signals or actual capacity.

Open this step →

4 · Pay the commitments

Can the court afford to stay, leave or return?

Local receipts and pledged outside deliveries must cover ritual and court bills. The court can leave after repeated unpaid bills. A separate rule determines whether adequate funding permits return.

Open this step →

5 · Test a published decline account

What changes when the documented climate sequence is applied?

Buckley’s regional drought proxy changes agricultural conditions after 1250 in the existing long-run social engine. The comparison uses the same parameters with neutral climate after 1250.

Open this step →

What the economy has to account for

Households need food. Fields and waterways need labour. The centre also has to provision builders, soldiers and ritual obligations. Infrastructure can improve future production while creating maintenance costs. These resource claims are the thread through the sequence.
